name: diagram
description: Draw, select and edit Mermaid diagrams and Apache ECharts charts beside VS Code chat.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Charts of a shell command's output are only available in trusted workspaces.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Charts of a shell command's output are not available in virtual workspaces.

chatParticipants.name: diagram
chatParticipants.description: Draw, change and explain diagrams and charts

commands.name: new
commands.description: Start a new diagram or chart instead of changing the current one

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain the current diagram or chart, or the selected parts

disambiguation.description: The user wants to draw, visualize, update or explain a diagram, such as a flowchart, sequence diagram, class diagram, state machine, entity relationship diagram, architecture overview, mind map, timeline or Gantt chart.
examples: Draw a sequence diagram of the login flow
Visualize the class hierarchy in this file
Make a flowchart of this algorithm
Add error handling to the diagram

disambiguation.description: The user wants to visualize data as a chart, such as a pie chart, bar chart, line chart, scatter plot, treemap, sankey, heatmap, radar chart, box plot, gauge or funnel, with the data given inline, in a file or as the output of a shell command.
examples: Render this data as a pie chart
Bar chart of the lines of code per folder
Plot the CSV file as a line chart
Show the disk usage of these directories as a pie chart
Treemap of the file sizes under src

languageModelTools.name: diagram_render
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show a Mermaid diagram or an ECharts chart in an interactive panel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Render Mermaid diagrams (structure and flow: flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, Gantt, mind map) or Apache ECharts 6 charts (quantitative data, language "echarts"). Replaces the diagram beside chat; users can select items, edit source and send follow-ups. Mermaid nodes can open code through "links". Returns success or an error to fix. For data files or command output, use diagram_chart.

source.description: Complete Mermaid source or ECharts option, without a code fence or diff. ECharts accepts JSON or a JavaScript object literal with callbacks (formatter, renderItem, symbolSize, labelLayout, etc.), including custom series. Prefer string templates such as "{b}: {c}" for plain formatters. Omit click directives, HTML, colors, backgrounds and fonts; the panel handles theming and chart sizing.

language.description: How the source is written. Defaults to "mermaid".

title.description: A short title for the diagram, shown in the panel.

clickPrompt.description: A single click immediately sends this request to chat on the user's behalf, replacing {label} with the node label or chart item name, e.g. "Explain {label} in more detail". Use for explorable overviews.

links.description: Map exact Mermaid node ids to file paths, absolute or relative to the first workspace folder, with optional lines: {"parse": "src/parser.ts#L42", "check": "src/checker.ts#L10-L30", "cli": "src/cli.ts"}. Clicking opens that location. Link nodes to code you have read. Mermaid only.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_chart
languageModelTools.userDescription: Chart data given inline, in a file or as a command's output
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Chart data with Apache ECharts, replacing the diagram beside chat. Supply exactly one of "data" (inline), "file" or "command" (shell output), e.g. a pie chart, plot of sales.csv, bar chart of lines per folder, or treemap of du -ah src. Returns how the data was interpreted. For full option control or callbacks such as custom-series renderItem, use diagram_render.

type.description: horizontalBar suits long labels; scatter compares the first two value columns; treemap/sunburst nest paths or label columns and sum children; sankey connects source/target columns or labels to a node per value column; heatmap pivots two label columns or uses value columns as columns; radar has an axis per value column; boxplot shows each group's spread; gauge shows one value; funnel orders stages by value.

title.description: A short title for the chart, shown in the panel.

data.description: Inline data: CSV, TSV, JSON (an array of objects or arrays, an object mapping names to numbers, or JSON Lines), a Markdown table or whitespace-separated columns.

file.description: Path to a file with the data, absolute or relative to the first workspace folder.

command.description: A shell command whose standard output is the data, run with /bin/sh (cmd.exe on Windows) in the first workspace folder. The user is asked to confirm it.

format.description: Defaults to "auto" detection, required for Markdown tables. "json" also reads JSON Lines.

labelColumn.description: Label column by header or generated name, e.g. "Column 2"; defaults to the first text column naming each row. Multiple names, outermost first, define treemap/sunburst levels, sankey stages (source, target), or heatmap rows/columns. Treemap, sunburst and sankey also split paths such as "src/webview/main.ts" into levels. Bar, line, area and scatter charts use ISO dates ("2026-01-02", "2026-01-02T14:30:00Z", "2026-01") as a time axis with proportional spacing. Ambiguous dates ("01/02/2026") and plain years remain labels.

valueColumns.description: Value columns, one series each. Defaults to numeric columns, excluding identifiers (id, rank, pid, etc.) and units differing from the first. Pie, treemap, sunburst, gauge and funnel use only the first; boxplot uses its raw numbers.

max.description: The top of a gauge's scale, or of every axis of a radar chart, in input units (bytes for sizes). Inferred from the data when left out: 100 for percentages, the total of the column, or rounded up from the value.

aggregate.description: Combine rows sharing the same label or labels. "count" counts rows without a value column, e.g. one row per commit or log entry. Grouping precedes "sort" and "limit"; sort descending to keep the largest groups. Omit for boxplot, which summarizes raw groups itself.

sort.description: Sorts the rows by the first value column, after grouping.

limit.description: Keep the first rows after sorting. Pie/doughnut exclude nonpositive values and combine omitted positive rows as "Other".

options.description: Merge an ECharts option: objects merge, null removes a setting, other values replace it. A "series" object applies to every series; an array of objects merges element by element, e.g. {"series": [{"label": {"show": false}}]}. Omit colors, backgrounds and fonts. JSON only; for callbacks use diagram_render with a JavaScript option.

clickPrompt.description: A single click on a chart item immediately sends this request to the chat on the user's behalf, with {label} replaced by the item's name, e.g. "Which files make {label} so large?".

languageModelTools.name: diagram_getState
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read the diagram shown in the diagram panel, with your edits and selection
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read the current diagram or chart: Mermaid source or ECharts JSON/JavaScript, manual edits, render errors and selected nodes/items. Call before changing a diagram or when the user refers to "this", "these" or selected parts. Lists selectable flowchart edges and sequence messages with exact relationship ids and endpoints for annotation.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_pickNodes
languageModelTools.userDescription: Ask you to select nodes, relationships or chart items in the diagram panel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Ask the user to select diagram nodes or chart items and wait for their answer, e.g. "Which step is failing?". Returns picked labels and ids, or why none was picked. First render with diagram_render or diagram_chart. Mermaid flowchart edges and sequence messages are also selectable; picked relationships include ids and endpoints.

prompt.description: One short question, shown above the diagram, e.g. 'Which part would you like to learn more about?'

multiple.description: Whether the user may pick several nodes, confirming with a Done button. Defaults to false: the first click answers.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_annotate
languageModelTools.userDescription: Mark nodes, flowchart edges, sequence messages or chart items without drawing again
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Mark existing nodes or chart items for walkthroughs, problems or paths without redrawing or moving the diagram. Each call replaces all marks; include every mark to keep, or omit marks to clear them. Marks do not change the source and clear on a new diagram. Returns marked and unknown ids. For flowchart edges and sequence messages, read exact edge:/message: relationship ids using diagram_getState; pass those ids in marks.

id.description: Exact Mermaid node id, edge:/message: relationship id, or chart item name reported by the panel. Call diagram_getState first; relationship ids may change when source changes.

mark.description: Theme-colored mark: "current" (default) for the step being explained, "problem" for a failure, "good" for something working or a recommended path, "info" for a pointer.

note.description: A short note about this node, at most 120 characters, shown above the diagram after the node's label, e.g. "times out after 30 s".

marks.description: Up to 50 node marks, replacing all previous marks. Omit or pass [] to clear.

caption.description: One short line shown above the diagram, at most 120 characters, e.g. "Step 2 of 3: the request is retried here".

dim.description: Fade unmarked items to emphasize marked nodes or paths. Defaults to false.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_findFiles
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find workspace files by glob before reading code to diagram. Returns bounded paths suitable for diagram_readFile and code links; reports truncation. Searches all workspace folders.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find workspace files by glob before reading code to diagram. Returns bounded paths suitable for diagram_readFile and code links; reports truncation. Searches all workspace folders.

glob.description: Workspace-relative glob, e.g. **/*.ts or src/**. Defaults to **/*. Honors files.exclude and search.exclude and omits .git and node_modules.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_searchText
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search a literal string in workspace text files, including unsaved open documents. Returns bounded matching lines with paths and line numbers. Narrow the glob when results or scanned files are truncated.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search a literal string in workspace text files, including unsaved open documents. Returns bounded matching lines with paths and line numbers. Narrow the glob when results or scanned files are truncated.

query.description: Single-line literal text to find, not a regular expression.

glob.description: Workspace-relative glob, e.g. **/*.ts or src/**. Defaults to **/*. Honors files.exclude and search.exclude and omits .git and node_modules.

maxResults.description: Maximum matching lines returned; defaults to 50.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_readFile
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read a bounded line range from a workspace text file, including unsaved editor changes. Returns numbered lines for understanding code and linking diagram nodes. Only files inside an open workspace are accepted.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read a bounded line range from a workspace text file, including unsaved editor changes. Returns numbered lines for understanding code and linking diagram nodes. Only files inside an open workspace are accepted.

file.description: Absolute path or URI from diagram_findFiles/diagram_searchText, or a path relative to the first workspace folder.

startLine.description: First line, inclusive and 1-based; defaults to 1.

endLine.description: Last line, inclusive; defaults to startLine + 199. At most 500 lines per read.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_inspectData
languageModelTools.userDescription: Inspect columns and sample rows from the current chart or another data source
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Inspect data without rendering or changing the current diagram. Omit the source to inspect the current chart's loaded data without reloading it, or supply exactly one of data, file or command. Returns column names and inferred types, row count and a bounded sample. Commands and external file access require the same confirmation as diagram_chart. Inspection of an explicit source and subsequent charting load the source separately.

data.description: Inline data: CSV, TSV, JSON (an array of objects or arrays, an object mapping names to numbers, or JSON Lines), a Markdown table or whitespace-separated columns.

file.description: Path to a file with the data, absolute or relative to the first workspace folder.

command.description: A shell command whose standard output is the data, run with /bin/sh (cmd.exe on Windows) in the first workspace folder. The user is asked to confirm it.

format.description: Defaults to "auto" detection, required for Markdown tables. "json" also reads JSON Lines.

sampleRows.description: Number of sample rows, defaults to 5. Samples may be shortened to fit output limits.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_updateChart
languageModelTools.userDescription: Change the current generated chart using its already loaded data, preserving supported manual presentation edits. Omitted fields are kept. Does not reload files or rerun commands. Use diagram_chart for a new data source; use Refresh in the panel if data is unavailable after reload. Unsupported manual source changes are preserved and block the update.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Change the current generated chart using its already loaded data, preserving supported manual presentation edits. Omitted fields are kept. Does not reload files or rerun commands. Use diagram_chart for a new data source; use Refresh in the panel if data is unavailable after reload. Unsupported manual source changes are preserved and block the update.

revision.description: Revision from diagram_getState; rejects stale updates when provided.

diagram.codeLens.enabled.markdownDescription: Show an **Open in Diagram** action above every `mermaid` and `echarts` code block in a Markdown file, which opens the diagram in the panel. The **Diagram: Open Diagram at Cursor** command opens one without it.
